app.name: Posthouse
app.tagline: Shared, versioned memory for all your AI agents
login.title: Sign in
login.subtitle: Enter the admin password to manage workspaces.
common.name: Name
ws.title: Workspaces
ws.empty: No workspaces yet. Create one, or let an agent create one through MCP or the skill.
ws.nameHint: Letters, digits, . _ - (any language). Example: paper-2026 or 论文项目
ws.passwordHint: Optional. Anyone with this password can read and write this workspace only.
ws.template: Add the standard layout (AGENTS.md, STATUS.md, DECISIONS.md, journal/, memory/, files/)
files.selectFile: Select a file on the left, or create a new one.
files.binary: Binary file ({size}). Download it to view.
files.deleteConfirm: Delete '{path}'? It stays recoverable from history.
files.conflict: This file was changed by someone else since you opened it.
files.leave: You have unsaved changes. Leave anyway?
settings.passwordSet: This workspace has its own password.
settings.passwordUnset: This workspace has no password of its own; only the admin and agent passwords can open it.
settings.compactHint: History is compacted automatically every day. Nothing is deleted; every old version stays available.
settings.compactHintHours: History is compacted automatically every {hours} hours. Nothing is deleted; every old version stays available.
settings.compactHintOff: Automatic compaction is off (POSTHOUSE_GIT_GC_HOURS=0). Nothing is deleted; every old version stays available.
settings.deleteText: Moves the workspace to the trash. Connections and tokens limited to it are revoked.
settings.deleteConfirm: Type the workspace name to confirm
connect.title: Connect agents
connect.intro: Every agent reaches this server through MCP (web apps, CLIs) or the REST API (the skill / curl). Pick the method your app supports.
connect.oauthTitle: Option A — Sign in with a password (recommended)
connect.oauthText: Add the MCP URL as a custom connector / app. When the app opens the sign-in page, enter a password. Leave Workspace empty for full access, or enter a workspace name to limit the connection to it.
connect.tokenTitle: Option B — Secret URL with a token
connect.tokenText: For apps that only accept a URL with no sign-in: create a token and use the URL that contains it. Anyone with the URL has access, so keep it private and revoke it when done.
connect.headerTitle: Option C — Header (CLI agents, Claude request headers)
connect.skillText: Agents with a shell (Claude Cowork, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) can use the bundled skill or plain curl.
connect.promptTitle: Starter prompt for a new conversation
connect.prompt: You can use the "Posthouse" connector. Our project lives in the workspace "{ws}". First call start_session(workspace="{ws}") and read AGENTS.md and STATUS.md. Keep STATUS.md current and call log_progress before you stop.
connect.createToken: Create a token for this workspace
connect.claude: Claude (web/desktop/mobile): Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
connect.chatgpt: ChatGPT (web): Settings → Security → turn on Developer mode, then Apps/Plugins → + (Add). Select it in each new chat.
connect.gemini: Gemini (web, where available): Settings → Connected apps → Add a custom app.
connect.cli: Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http posthouse {url} — Codex / Gemini CLI: add the URL to the MCP settings file (see docs).
tokens.title: Access tokens
tokens.intro: Tokens are revocable credentials for agents. Use them as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' or inside the secret MCP URL.
tokens.created: Token created — copy it now, it will not be shown again.
tokens.urlWithToken: MCP URL with token (no sign-in needed)
tokens.nameHint: Shown as the author of changes, e.g. ChatGPT
tokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke token '{name}'? Apps using it will lose access.
conn.title: Connected apps
conn.intro: Apps that signed in through OAuth (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini…). Revoke to disconnect.
activity.title: Activity
trash.title: Trash
trash.intro: Deleted workspaces. Restore them or delete them forever.
trash.purgeConfirm: Permanently delete '{name}'? This cannot be undone.
oauth.title: Authorize access
oauth.wants: {client} wants to read and write your workspaces.
oauth.loopback: This app runs on a local computer. Only allow it if you started it yourself.
oauth.help: Admin or agent password: leave Workspace empty for full access, or enter a workspace name to limit this connection to that workspace. Workspace password: enter that workspace's name.
common.copyManually: Press Ctrl+C (⌘C on a Mac) to copy the selected text.
setup.title: Set up a new Claude task
setup.cardText: For Cowork and Claude Code: one message that installs the Posthouse skill, signs in, turns on automatic conversation saving and loads the project.
setup.intro: This creates a token that opens only “{ws}” and a message with the server address and that token. Paste the message as the first message of a new Cowork or Claude Code task. Claude then installs the skill, signs in, saves the conversation to the workspace before and after every turn, and loads the project.
setup.copied: Copied. Paste it into a new Claude task.
setup.tokenNote: Created the token “{name}”. Anyone with this message can read and write this workspace. Revoke the token under Tokens when you no longer need it.
setup.httpWarning: The server address in the message is {url}. Claude's cloud sandboxes usually reach only HTTPS sites on port 443, so set POSTHOUSE_PUBLIC_URL to your public HTTPS address (see docs/deploy.md).
setup.msgIntro: Please connect this task to my Posthouse workspace "{ws}" and save our conversation there automatically, before and after every turn.
setup.msgTokenNote: (opens only this workspace; never copy it into workspace files or summaries)
setup.msgRun: Run these commands (macOS or Linux shell):
setup.msgAfter: Then follow the Posthouse skill in ~/.claude/skills/posthouse/SKILL.md and tell me in a few lines where the project stands. Automatic saving uses Claude Code hooks, so it works in Claude Code and Cowork. Anywhere else, skip install-hooks and just use the workspace.
skill.title: Agent skill
skill.text: Teaches Claude and other agents how to use your workspaces, with a small command-line tool (Python, no dependencies). It also installs the conversation auto-save hooks for Claude Code.
skill.claudeApp: claude.ai, the Claude desktop app and Cowork: download the zip and upload it under Skills in Claude's settings. Every chat and task can then use it.
skill.claudeCode: Claude Code: run this on the computer where Claude Code runs:
setup.allOption: All workspaces (Claude picks or creates one)
setup.introAll: This creates a token with agent access and a message with the server address and that token. Paste it as the first message of a new Cowork or Claude Code task. Claude installs the skill and signs in, asks which project you are working on (or creates a workspace for it), turns on automatic conversation saving and loads the project.
setup.allWarning: This token can read and write every workspace and create new ones. For a single project, use the Setup message button on that workspace: its token opens only that workspace.
setup.emptyHint: Copy a setup message into a new Claude task and Claude creates the workspace for your project.
setup.msgIntroServer: Please connect this task to my Posthouse server, where my AI agents share project files and memory, and save our conversation to the project's workspace automatically, before and after every turn.
setup.msgTokenNoteAgent: (agent access: can list, create, read and write all workspaces; never copy it into workspace files or summaries)
setup.msgAfterServer: Then follow the Posthouse skill in ~/.claude/skills/posthouse/SKILL.md. Ask me which project we are working on and use its workspace, or create one with `{cli} create NAME -d "short description"`. Then run `{cli} install-hooks --workspace NAME` so our conversation is saved there before and after every turn, run `{cli} start NAME`, and tell me in a few lines where the project stands. Automatic saving uses Claude Code hooks, so it works in Claude Code and Cowork. Anywhere else, skip install-hooks.
server.title: Settings
server.summary: {n} workspaces · files {files} · change history {history} · trash {trash} · database {db}
server.compactAllHint: Nothing is deleted; every old version stays available.
server.gitOff: Version history is off (POSTHOUSE_GIT=false), so there is nothing to compact.
server.publicUrlUnset: Not set; taken from each request (now {url})
server.publicUrlWarning: Agents reach this server at {url}. Claude's cloud sandboxes and the web apps need an HTTPS address on port 443: set POSTHOUSE_PUBLIC_URL (see docs/deploy.md).
server.loginLimitValue: {n} failures per {m} minutes per IP address
server.howToChange: These values come from the .env file in the Posthouse folder. To change one, edit .env and run ./scripts/docker-start.sh restart (or sudo systemctl restart posthouse). Passwords are not shown here: ./scripts/docker-start.sh passwords prints them on the server.
